To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) AMLR reactivities of CD4+ but not CD8+ T lymphocytes are impaired in patients with active rheumatoid arthritis; and (2) this impairment can be partially corrected by physiological concentrations of IL2.
AMLR reactivities of CD4+ but not CD8+ T-cell subsets were reduced in rheumatoid patients with low AMLR reactivites, but that these responses could be reconstituted by exogenous IL-2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of T cell subsets in the pathophysiology of rheumatoid arthritis and with the possibility of developing a T cell subset-based diagnostic assay for RA.
the hypothesis that impaired AMLR of T cells in rheumatoid synovial fluid (SF) is a consequence of the pathogenesis of rheumatoid arthritis, rather than an epiphenomenon.
the possibility that impaired autologous mixed leukocyte reaction (AMRL) reactivity of CD8+ T lymphocytes may play a role in the pathogenesis of rheumatoid arthritis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AMLR reactivities of CD4 and CD8 T cell subsets from RA patients are impaired and may be partially restored by IL-2.
the impaired AMLR of T cells in rheumatoid patients is not related to pre-activation of these cells.

the AMLR reactivitiy of CD4+ cells is impaired in the majority of patients with active disease, and that the AMLRs of CD8+ T lymphocytes are also impaired, but only in a subgroup of patients with severe active disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the impaired AMLR of RA patients was due to an intrinsic defect in the CD4+ T subset and the CD8+ T subset, and that the defect was more profound in the CD8+ subset.
the CD4 T cells of RA patients are functionally abnormal, but that the CD8 T cells are not.
impaired AMLR is associated with RA, and this impairment may be due to a defect in IL-2 production.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the AMLR is a useful tool to examine T cell reactivity in RA.
the AMLR assay is a useful tool for assessing the immune status of RA patients.
there are different pathophysiological processes at work in RA that can affect T cell reactivity.
